sq.QUESTION_DESC: Find the half range sine series for \(f(x)=x(\pi - x)\) in \((0, \pi)\).
Find the half range cosine series for \(f(x)=x\) in \((0, \pi)\).

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Extend } f(x) \text{ as even function to } (-L, L)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Half-range cosine series: } f(x) = \frac{a_0}{2} + \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} a_n \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L})\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{where: } a_0 = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L} f(x) dx\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L} f(x) \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L}) dx\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Define half-range cosine series for } f(x) \text{ in } (0, L).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L} x dx = L\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{2}{L} \int_0^{L} x \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L}) dx = \frac{2L}{n^2\pi^2}[(-1)^n - 1]\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{For even } n: a_n = 0; \text{ for odd } n: a_n = -\frac{4L}{n^2\pi^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } x = \frac{L}{2} - \frac{4L}{\pi^2}\sum_{n=\text{odd}} \frac{1}{n^2} \cos(\frac{n\pi x}{L})\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Find half-range cosine series for } f(x) = x \text{ in } (0, L).\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Because function defined only on half the interval } (0, L) \text{ of length } L\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{But Fourier series has period } 2L, \text{ which is double the original interval}\)

(3 Mark)

\(\text{Thus interval of definition is half the period of Fourier series}\)

(2 Mark)

Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Define } f_e(x) = \begin{cases} f(x) & 0 \leq x \leq L \\ f(-x) & -L \leq x \leq 0 \end{cases}\)

(4 Mark)

\(\text{This makes } f_e(x) \text{ even function in } (-L, L)\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Fourier series of } f_e(x) \text{ is cosine series representing } f(x) \text{ in } (0, L)\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{What is even extension of function for half-range cosine series?}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(a_0 = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} \sin x dx = \frac{4}{\pi}\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_n = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} \sin x \cos nx dx = \frac{2}{\pi} \cdot \frac{1 + (-1)^n}{1 - n^2} \text{ for } n \neq 1\)

(2 Mark)

\(a_1 = \frac{2}{\pi} \int_0^{\pi} \sin x \cos x dx = 0\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Thus } \sin x = \frac{2}{\pi} - \frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=\text{even}} \frac{\cos nx}{n^2 - 1}\)

(2 Mark)

lq.QUESTION_DESC: Find the half-range cosine series for \(f(x)=x(\pi-x)\) in \((0,\pi)\). Hence, evaluate \(\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{1}{n^4}\).

lq.ANSWER:
StepMarks
Cosine series: \(\sin x=\frac{a_0}{2}+\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}a_n\cos nx\)(1)
\(a_0=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\,dx=\frac{4}{\pi}\)(2)
\(a_n=\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi}\sin x\cos nx\,dx=\frac{2}{\pi}\cdot\frac{1+(-1)^n}{1-n^2}\) for \(n\neq1\)(4)
\(a_1=0\)(2)
Thus, \(\sin x=\frac{2}{\pi}-\frac{4}{\pi}\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{\cos 2nx}{4n^2-1}\)(4)
